<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 10:6:8">Y. Ter. X, 47ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>אנא מה דשַׁמְעִית ואינון מה דשַׁמְעוּן</he> I report what I have heard, and they, what they have heard.
Sabb. 46ᵇ הא שַׁמְעִינָן ליה לר״ש וכ׳ have we not heard what R. S. says &c.? Y. Sot. VII, beg. 21ᵇ, v. אֲלִנִיסְטִי; a. v. fr.—שמיע ל־ he has heard, he knows of.

<cite ref="Eruvin 9b:7">Erub. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>ור״י מי לא ש׳ ליה הא</he> but has R. J. not heard that (does he not know that Boraitha of R. Ḥiya)? <he>ש׳ ליה ולא סבר</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) he knows of it, but does not accept it.
<cite ref="Eruvin 10a:8">Ib. 10ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>לא ש׳ לי הא שמעתתא</he> this tradition is not known to me.
Pes. 34ᵃ מידי ש׳ לך בהא do you know anything about this (hălakhah)?; a. v. fr.—Esp. שמע מ־ to understand from, to infer, prove.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 72b:6">Ab. Zar. 72ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ש׳ מינה וכ׳</he> (abbrev. <he>ש״מ</he>) deduce from this that &c.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 72b:6">Ib.</cite> <he>שַׁמְעַת מינה וכ׳</he> wilt thou conclude from this that &c.? <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 72b:6">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>אלא מהא ליכא למִשְׁמַע מינה</he> but (the conclusion is,) you can derive nothing from this.—
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 72b:6">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>תא שמע</he> (abbrev. <he>ת״ש</he>; v. <cite ref="A03397"><he>אֲתָא</he></cite>) come and learn, i.e. derive it from the following.
Sabb. 13ᵇ ת״ש … ש״מ ואלו תנן ש״מ I will prove it (from this Tosefta): ‘you must not …, and those are some of the halakhoth &c.’, which proves that the right version is ‘and those’: it stands proved.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5:21">Y. M. Kat. III, 83ᵃ</cite> top <he>נִישְׁמְעִינָהּ מן הדא</he> let us prove it from this; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to give to understand; to teach, prove.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 2a:8">Ber. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>מילתא … קא מַשְׁמַע לן וכ׳</he> (the Tannai in using such an expression) wants to teach us something by the way: when do the priests eat &c.; <he>והא קמשמע לן וכ׳</he> (abbrev. <he>קמ״ל</he>) and it is this he teaches us, that the sacrifice of atonement is not indispensable &c. Ib. 4ᵇ <he>לאפוקי … קמ״ל דחובה</he> in opposition to the opinion that the evening prayer is optional, he gives us to understand that it is obligatory.

<cite ref="Shabbat 19a:3">Sabb. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>מהו דתימא … קמ״ל</he> you may have thought (that the cases are different, because) this devolves upon him, and the other does not, therefore he teaches us (that they are the same).
Ib. 108ᵃ מאי קמ״ל what does he teach us (is it not a matter of course)? Ber. 21ᵃ sq. דאי אַשְׁמְעִינָן וכ׳, v. צְרִיךְ; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. מַשְׁמֵע a) understood.
Yeb. 102ᵇ מ׳ הכי ומ׳ הכי it may be understood thus (it may mean, ‘to take off’), and may be understood thus (it may mean, ‘to strengthen’); a. fr.—2) inferred, proved; evidence.

<cite ref="Shabbat 84b:5">Sabb. 84ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי מ׳</he> how is this proved (from the verse quoted)? <cite ref="Eruvin 65a:6">Erub. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>מאי מ׳ וכ׳</he> what evidence is there &c.?, v. <cite ref="Q00314"><he>פּוּק</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 65a:6">Ib.</cite> <he>מַשְׁמְעֵי</he>, v. infra; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="M02925"><he>מַשְׁמָע</he></cite>.
